# Exact period-three sector compression and two domination obstructions

This note retains actual convex-body data and the full sector PSD criterion.
It proves an exact three-dimensional compression and gives actual triangle
counterexamples to two tempting ways of turning it into the cubic matrix.
Neither counterexample violates the cubic inequality itself.

## 1. Exact compressed matrix

Use the six canonical rays

    (1,0),(0,1),(-1,1),(-1,0),(0,-1),(1,-1).

Let their actual positive scalar radii be R_i and their consecutive sector
areas be W_i. Write c_i=1/(2W_i). The exact six-sector matrix L satisfies,
after substituting z_i=R_i x_i,

    z^T L z=sum_i c_i(R_i x_i+R_(i+1)x_(i+1))^2
                      -sum_i x_i^2-2sum_i x_i x_(i+1). (1)

All indices on six nodes are cyclic. On the period-three subspace
x_(i+3)=x_i, the last two sums equal 2(x_0+x_1+x_2)^2. Thus the exact
compressed symmetric matrix N is PSD and has

    N_ii=R_i^2(c_(i-1)+c_i)
                +R_(i+3)^2(c_(i+2)+c_(i+3))-2,

    N_i,i+1=c_i R_i R_(i+1)
                +c_(i+3)R_(i+3)R_(i+4)-2.           (2)

Here indices on N are modulo three. Each adjacent canonical ray pair has
determinant one. The core inequalities therefore imply
c_i R_i R_(i+1)<=1, and consequently every off-diagonal entry of N is
nonpositive. This really is a three-by-three symmetric Z-matrix obtained
by an exact congruence from the actual L.

## 2. Singularity criterion at a strict-incidence triangle

Let the actual triangle's signed vertex matrix have positive diagonal a_i
and negative off-diagonal entries -b_ij, all b_ij>0. Its three unique-sector
blocks in L are singular two-node blocks; its double-sector edges are
cores. If a unique vertex is uP+vQ between its two actual ray endpoints,
that block has kernel ratio (v,u).

In coordinates x_i=z_i/R_i the three kernel ratios become

    x_5/x_0=b_31/b_21,
    x_1/x_2=b_12/b_32,
    x_3/x_4=b_23/b_13.                               (3)

For example P_1=(a_1,-b_21) has coefficients
u=b_21/R_5 and v=b_31/R_0 on rays 5,0, since a_1=b_21+b_31.
Dividing the kernel coordinates by their respective radii gives the
first ratio; the others follow in the same way.

On the period-three subspace, x_3=x_0, x_4=x_1, x_5=x_2. Hence it
meets ker L nontrivially if and only if

    b_12 b_23 b_31=b_13 b_32 b_21.                    (4)

All coefficients are positive, so if (4) holds that intersection is
one-dimensional, and if it fails the intersection is zero. Since L is
PSD, its quadratic form vanishes exactly on its kernel. Consequently N
is singular exactly when (4) holds, and otherwise N is positive definite.

Condition (4) is NOT the edge-drop cycle balance characterizing cubic
equality. It depends on source placement even though the triangle's
strict-incidence f-vector is independent of that placement.

## 3. An actual cubic-tight triangle with positive definite compression

Take

    P_1=(87/100,-49/100),
    P_2=(-1/200,1/100),
    P_3=(-1/200,-23/200)

and the canonical normals (1,0),(0,1),(-1,-1) at zero. The positive
diagonal is (87/100,1/100,3/25), and the off-diagonal magnitudes are

    b_12=b_13=1/200,
    b_21=49/100, b_23=23/200,
    b_31=19/50, b_32=1/200.

The columns balance, the positive principal cofactors put zero strictly
inside the triangle, and all three cuts strictly isolate their vertices.
Its exact ordinary vector is

    f=(7/4,1/2,1/2),       sum f_i^2+prod f_i=4.

But the ratio of the two sides in (4) is 874/49, so N is positive
definite. The following explicit actual data provide a direct rational
certificate as well:

    R=(1/80,1/140,1/200,1/200,41/350,41/200),
    W=(1/22400,17/560000,1/80000,
                             13/22400,1681/140000,3361/80000).

Formula (2) gives

    N=[[844802/1092325, -161/325,       -6517/6722],
       [-161/325,       65226/5525,    -7/17],
       [-6517/6722,     -7/17,         379827/228548]].

Its leading principal minors are respectively

    844802/1092325,
    164990791/18569525,
    9338175/2971124,

all strictly positive.

Normalize N to diagonal one and let r_ij=-N_ij/sqrt(N_ii N_jj).
There is NO assignment of the three target numbers f_i/2 to its edges
such that f_i/2<=r_ij on every edge. If such an assignment existed, the
target matrix C(f) with diagonal one and those negative off-diagonals
would be positive definite: for every nonzero real w,

    w^T C(f)w >=|w|^T C(f)|w|
                 >=|w|^T normalized(N)|w|>0.

That contradicts det C(f)=0. This excludes the proposed normalized
entrywise domination even on actual positive, cubic-tight triangle data,
independently of the chosen fixed cap-to-edge indexing.

## 4. Opposite-area Cauchy aggregation can even destroy PSD

For the simpler triangle conv{(2,-1),(-1,2),(-1,-1)}, all R_i=1,
the W_i alternate 1/2,1, and all opposite chord sums sigma_i=2.
Its exact compressed energy is

    sum_i x_i^2-sum_(i<j) x_i x_j>=0.

A natural lower bound for each pair of opposite positive terms in (1)
would replace them by

    (sigma_i x_i+sigma_(i+1)x_(i+1))^2
                                      /[2(W_i+W_(i+3))].

After the same negative term is subtracted, this produces

    (2/3)sum_i x_i^2-(4/3)sum_(i<j) x_i x_j,

which equals -2 at x=(1,1,1). Thus this aggregated matrix is not PSD,
despite actual convexity, exact core signs, and L>=0. Cauchy supplies a
lower bound for the positive energy, not an implication that the lowered
energy remains nonnegative.

These obstructions leave open a different Schur minimization or a
compression retaining additional opposite-ray variables. They rule out
only the displayed natural shortcuts, with exact actual-body certificates.
